Siblings: Meritorius and his brother; the son and the daughter. By (i) the daughter and the brother share a column, so Meritorius and the son share the other column.

By (ii) the son is diagonal to the sibling of the worst orator. The worst orator cannot be the daughter (the son would have to be diagonal to himself), and cannot be the brother (the son would have to be diagonal to Meritorius, who is in his own column).

Worst = son: the son is diagonal to the daughter, so the brother sits in the son's row. Worst = Meritorius: the son is diagonal to the brother, so the brother sits in Meritorius' row.

In both cases (iii) puts the best orator in the worst orator's row, and that seat is the brother's. The best orator is Meritorius' brother.
